A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Logic Networks research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including relocated material and the new Appendix D.4.

before.justification: V5 reports original Boolean-network discovery, tabular classification, medical and cybersecurity results, plus the simulation comparing independence assumptions in Appendix B.1.3.

after.justification: V6 retains those original results and adds experiments comparing discretization heuristics and rule reset in Appendix D.4.

M1.justification: The signed AND/OR nodes, biases, factorized rule modules, training, reset mechanism and missing-value handling remain unchanged. All four greedy discretization algorithms were already documented in v5; v6 evaluates them without replacing the method.

E1.justification: The datasets and tasks are retained. The new ablation uses tic-tac-toe, chess, monk2, kidney and wine, all previously evaluated; it introduces no new domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table D.2 newly reports threshold discretization and no-discretization controls alongside the existing greedy heuristics. Comparator membership in the original tabular, Boolean-network and cybersecurity comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a controlled evaluation of six discretization conditions with reset enabled and two conditions with reset disabled, using five-fold cross-validation. The original benchmark splits, metrics, model capacities and procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3 and D.4 add systematic ablations addressing which discretization heuristic works best and whether rule reset is useful. This supplies substantial quantitative validation of two central pipeline choices previously lacking such comparisons. Earlier supplementary analyses and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Beyond v5's existing repetition descriptions, v6 reports ten random seeds per ablation configuration and means and standard deviations across seed-specific five-fold scores. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting and explicitly distinguishes seed variability from configuration effects.

E6.justification: Table D.2 adds focused ablation results: with reset enabled, average F1 is 94.09% for thresholding, 94.85% for descending selection and 95.77% for additive discretization. These are new multi-seed results; the original benchmark values and case-study findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, independence assumptions, AND/OR formulations and Appendix B derivations and proofs are retained. V6 adds illustrative examples and explanations of existing assumptions and structural choices, without changing the formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain their central claims. Section 1.1 adds direct missing-value handling as a third claimed advantage over earlier NLN approaches, extending the stated comparative contribution.

C2.justification: V6 adds interpretations of discretization's computational tradeoff, reset's marginal usefulness and seed variability. It also explains the nonnegative OR design and adds specific discussion of discriminatory Adult-dataset rules, expert auditing and risks from spurious correlations.

D1.justification: Appendix D.4 explicitly identifies descending selection as the heuristic used for the retained experiments, clarifying their reproduction. The implementation description, numerical hyperparameters and Code Availability statement otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. V6 expands the contrast with previously cited NLN/RRL approaches concerning missing-value imputation and clarifies historical weight conventions, making a limited refinement to research positioning.

P1.justification: V6 divides Section 2.1 into three subsections, expands explanatory examples and adds ablation, broader-impact and author-contribution sections. These are localized expansions; most existing prose and the overall narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: V6 adds Table D.2, moves Figure 2 earlier into the probabilistic introduction and expands captions for Figures 1, 3, 4 and 5. Existing diagrams and plots retain their content, with limited placement and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: The ten-seed ablations provide useful evidence about previously unquantified pipeline choices, while clearer explanations and specific discussion of discriminatory rules improve the paper. The gains are limited by testing only the five strongest datasets and minor reporting inconsistencies: Appendix D.4 claims a maximum reset benefit of 0.25 percentage points, although Table D.2 shows 0.36 on Monk2.
